body: Cultural attitudes and social norms evolve over time, yet most cultural benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) treat culture as a static attribute of a country or region. We introduce ChronoCulture, a benchmark of 10,360 temporal pairs built from longitudinal survey data across 72 countries. Each pair contains the same survey question asked in the same country in an older and a newer year, with full population response distributions as ground truth. Across six LLMs, we find that models can often predict a country's attitudes at one point in time but do not reliably capture how those attitudes change. Their predictions for different years tend to stay close together, failing to capture much of the observed change. Specifying the intended year in the prompt also offers little overall improvement in alignment with survey responses. These findings suggest that models often present a largely static picture of cultural attitudes, highlighting the need to evaluate cultural awareness across time.
summaryZh: 文化态度和社会规范随时间演变，但现有的文化基准测试多将文化视为静态属性。本文引入了ChronoCulture基准，包含来自72个国家、涵盖10,360个时间对的纵向调查数据。对6个主流大模型的测试表明，模型虽然能预测特定时点的态度，但无法可靠地捕捉态度随时间的变化，提示未来需加强对模型动态文化意识的评估。
